data.content_ref: inline:The specified durable record is purely meta-temporal—causal timestamps and a happens-before proof—and omits any content-addressed reference to the completed evidence itself. Consequently the protocol can satisfy its own record-keeping requirement while the actual evidence is silently displaced from the reclaimed workspace. Moreover, because the crashed holder leaves no terminal record behind, the seal-emission timestamp and happens-before proof must reside in an external causal store that the target never identifies or justifies; the answer therefore evades the requirement to determine a concrete safest protocol by offering only an ungrounded comparative latency criterion.
